tags.name: Cave dive site
tags.qa_note: Locally known as 'Galapita Gala' cave. Coordinates are ~150m from 'Gala pita gala dive site' in this dataset; the two entries very likely describe the same real-world boulder/cave complex (or immediately adjacent parts of it), flagged here as a probable near-duplicate rather than merged. Entry type corrected from shore to boat (10-15 min boat ride from Unawatuna dive centers per sources). Re-audited 2026-09-25: all 3 prior sources re-confirmed live and unchanged; added divejourney.io as a 4th independent source, which describes the complex as a 'boat-run Unawatuna pinnacle' (an alternate characterization to the boulder-reef/cave description used by the other operators -- noted but site_type kept as cave/reef since only one of four sources uses 'pinnacle'). Crucially, divejourney.io site-specifically names green and hawksbill turtles and scorpionfish at this exact complex -- these were previously removed for lack of a site-specific source and are now restored to the marine-life section with this citation. Glassfish, shrimp, moray eels, and strong tidal cave-mouth currents remain unconfirmed by any source and stay removed.

tags.name: Conch dive site
tags.depth_range: 14m (bow) to 21m (stern); prior single value of ~22m was unsourced
tags.qa_note: SS Conch: 1892-built (completed by end of June 1892), 3,555-ton Shell tanker, built by W. Gray & Co, Stockton, dimensions 338.4 x 43 x 26.4 feet; struck rock off Akurala and broke in two carrying bulk oil cargo Novorossisk-Colombo-Madras. Sources conflict on exact sinking date (June 2 vs June 3, 1903) and the rock's exact name (Akurala/Akkurala/Akarta/Parsi-Passa gala) -- both conflicts stated explicitly in markdown rather than resolved by guessing. Re-audited 2026-09-25: archaeology.lk re-fetched and all figures (tonnage, dimensions, builder, date, depths) reconfirmed unchanged; it additionally states the wreck now spans roughly 100 x 35 meters across the seabed and has been 'damaged by explosions and looting over time' -- this is post-sinking salvage/looting damage, NOT a claim about the original 1903 sinking cause, and is kept clearly distinct from the still-unconfirmed single-source original 'explosion/dynamite as cause of sinking' claim. Added archive.roar.media as a 4th source, which independently corroborates only the wreck's existence/1903 date/Hikkaduwa-area location (no technical specifications) -- a weak but genuinely independent 4th corroboration. 'Queen angelfish' (non-Indian-Ocean species) remains removed as a likely copy-paste error from aggregator blogs.

tags.name: Carreg dive site
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-07-03 and again 2026-09-25: no shipwreck database, dive-shop wreck listing, maritime archive, or Wikipedia entry names a wreck called 'Carreg' anywhere off Sri Lanka despite extensive search across both audits. Coordinates place this near Negombo, not Hikkaduwa as an earlier markdown draft claimed (also corrected). The 2026-09-25 re-search additionally cross-checked known Negombo-area wreck rosters (Wreck Chief Dragon, Taprobane wreck, the 1945 aircraft-carrier wreck) from divesrilanka.com and srilanka-divingtours.com -- none is named or aliased 'Carreg'. Vessel name, build date, tonnage, and sinking cause remain all unverified and stay removed from the markdown; only the OSM historic=wreck/seamark:type=wreck tagging supports a wreck-like feature existing here at all. Remains downgraded from a prior 'validated: true' that was sourced only to the generic tag 'perplexity'.

tags.name: Goddamahagale dive site
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-07-03 and again 2026-09-25: coordinates are ~7km offshore WNW of Negombo (confirmed correct framing; a prior draft's 'near Kalutara/Beruwala/Bentota' correction was itself wrong and has been rejected). Name closely resembles 'Goda Maha Gala', named in Negombo operator site rosters, and a third-party database lists a 'Maha Gala' ~7.6km away -- plausibly related but not confirmed as the same site. The 2026-09-25 re-search found a further complication: PADI's dive-site listing for a similarly-named 'Goda Gala' (padi.com/dive-site/sri-lanka/goda-gala/) places THAT site at 6.075N 80.10355E, near Hikkaduwa -- over 130km south of these coordinates and clearly a different site entirely, confirming this name (and close variants) is reused for multiple, unrelated dive sites around Sri Lanka. This reinforces rather than resolves the identity uncertainty, so validated stays false. Entry type corrected from shore to boat (Negombo-area sites are consistently boat dives several km offshore). Fabricated claims of hard corals, sea fans, lionfish, scorpionfish, wrasse, reliable turtles, and reef octopus remain removed. Remains downgraded from a prior 'validated: true' sourced only to the generic tag 'perplexity'.
